name: Cotton ball diet

lead: The cotton ball diet involves swallowing cotton balls, often dipped in juice, in place of food to feel full.
It was reported as an online fad around 2013 and has been condemned by health professionals.

paras: The balls are meant to fill the stomach with a non-caloric bulk. Cotton is not digestible.
Reported risks include bezoars and intestinal obstruction needing surgery, malnutrition, choking, and concern that it signals disordered eating.

lead: The cotton ball diet is a fad diet in which people swallow cotton balls, sometimes dipped in juice or smoothies, to feel full without eating food. [1][2]
It was covered by news outlets in November 2013 and has been widely condemned by health professionals as dangerous, because cotton cannot be digested and may form blockages. [1][3]

paras: Practitioners ingest cotton balls, often soaked in juice, lemonade or smoothies, in place of meals. The aim is a sense of fullness from a non-caloric filler. [1][2]

The diet circulated on forums and video sites around 2013, and a June 2013 interview with model Bria Murphy was cited as drawing attention to it in fashion. News coverage appeared in November 2013. [1][2] It has no formal scientific or commercial backing. [2]

Reported dangers include intestinal blockage by a bezoar, a mass of undigested material that can cause pain, vomiting and bowel obstruction requiring emergency surgery, along with dehydration, malnutrition and choking. Many commercial cotton balls are bleached polyester rather than cotton, which commentators say raises concern about chemical residues. Experts quoted in coverage consider the practice a sign of an eating disorder. [1][2][3]
No studies found. A 2024 preprint discusses bezoar formation and serious consequences of eating cotton balls to fill the stomach. [3]

timeline.event: Practice reported on forums and in news coverage. [1][2]
